'''István Fáry''' (30 June 1922 – 2 November 1984) was a [[Hungarian people|Hungarian]]-born [[mathematician]] known for his work in [[geometry]] and [[algebraic topology]].<ref name="cdl">{{citation|author=[[S. S. Chern]], R. J. DeVogelaere, and [[Robion Kirby|R. C. Kirby]]|url=http://content.cdlib.org/xtf/view?docId=hb4d5nb20m&doc.view=frames&chunk.id=div00051&toc.depth=1&toc.id=|contribution=Istvan Fary, Mathematics: Berkeley|publisher=[[California Digital Library]]|year=1985|title=University of California: In Memoriam}}.</ref> He proved [[Fáry's theorem]] that every [[planar graph]] has a [[planar straight-line graph|straight-line embedding]] in 1948, and the [[Fáry–Milnor theorem]] lower-bounding the curvature of a nontrivial [[knot (mathematics)|knot]] in 1949.

==Biography==
Fáry was born June 30, 1922, in [[Gyula, Hungary]]. After studying for a master's degree at the [[University of Budapest]], he moved to the [[University of Szeged]], where he earned a Ph.D. in 1947. He then studied at the [[University of Paris|Sorbonne]] before taking a faculty position at the [[University of Montreal]] in 1955. He moved to the [[University of California, Berkeley]] in 1958 and became a full professor in 1962. He died on November 2, 1984, in [[El Cerrito, California]].<ref name="cdl"/>
